name: Conditionals
moduleIntroduction: Welcome to the Conditionals module! This is the grammar of 'What If'. In French, you say 'Si je viens' or 'Si je viendrai'. In English, we have strict rules. The biggest rule? You almost never put 'Will' or 'Would' in the same part of the sentence as 'If'.
contrastiveExplanation:
First Conditional (Real Future):
English: If + Present, ... Will.
French: Often uses Future logic in both parts.

Second Conditional (Imaginary):
English: If + Past Simple, ... Would. (Use 'Were' for I/He/She).
French: Uses Imparfait (Si j'avais).

Third Conditional (Regret):
English: If + Past Perfect, ... Would Have.
French: Si j'avais su...

commonErrors.wrong: If I will see him, I will tell him.
commonErrors.correct: If I see him, I will tell him.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Applying future logic to the 'if' clause. Never use 'will' after 'if'.

commonErrors.wrong: If I would have money, I would buy a car.
commonErrors.correct: If I had money, I would buy a car.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Common error even in French ('Si j'aurais'). Never use 'would' in the 'if' clause.

commonErrors.wrong: If I was you, I would accept.
commonErrors.correct: If I were you, I would accept.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Standard English uses the Subjunctive 'Were' for all persons in unreal situations.

commonErrors.wrong: Unless you don't study, you will fail.
commonErrors.correct: Unless you study, you will fail.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: French 'A moins que... ne...'. 'Unless' implies 'if not', so adding 'don't' creates a double negative.

commonErrors.wrong: If I knew, I would have come.
commonErrors.correct: If I had known, I would have come.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Confusing Past Simple (Knew) with Past Perfect (Had known) for past regrets.

items.questionText: If it rains, I ___ at home.
items.feedback: Correct! First Conditional: If + Present, ... Will.

items.questionText: If you ___ water, it boils.
items.feedback: Correct! Zero Conditional (Fact): If + Present, ... Present.

items.questionText: If she comes, we ___ happy.
items.feedback: Correct! Real possibility in the future.

items.questionText: I will call you if I ___ time.
items.feedback: Correct! The 'If' part takes the Present Simple.

items.questionText: Unless you ___, you will miss the bus.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Unless' means 'If you do not'. So we say 'Unless you run'.

items.questionText: If I miss the bus, I ___ a taxi.
Plants die if they ___ water.
If he ___, tell him to wait.
items.feedback: Correct! Present Simple (he calls) in the condition.

items.questionText: We will go to the beach if it ___ sunny.
___ you study, you will fail.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Unless' = 'If not'. (If you do not study...)

items.questionText: If you mix red and blue, you ___ purple.
What will you do if you ___ the exam?
If I see Ngono, I ___ her.
If you ___ hard, you will succeed.
You get wet if you ___ in the rain.
I will cook dinner if you ___ the dishes.
If the bus ___, we will walk.
If you are hungry, ___ an apple.
I won't go if you ___ come.
items.feedback: Correct! Negative condition in Present Simple.

items.questionText: If you drop a glass, it ___.
If I ___ rich, I would buy a big house.
items.feedback: Correct! Second Conditional (Imaginary). We use 'Were' for all persons.

items.questionText: If I ___ you, I would tell the truth.
items.feedback: Correct! 'If I were you' (Fixed advice phrase).

items.questionText: If he worked harder, he ___ pass.
I would travel if I ___ enough money.
items.feedback: Correct! Second Conditional (Unreal Present): If + Past Simple.

items.questionText: When I ___, I will call you.
items.feedback: Correct! Time clauses (When, As soon as) follow the same rule as 'If' (Present Simple for future).

items.questionText: If it ___, we would go for a walk.
items.feedback: Correct! Second Conditional negative: Past Simple (didn't).

items.questionText: What ___ you do if you lost your job?
items.feedback: Correct! 'Lost' is past, so we need 'Would'.

items.questionText: As soon as he ___, we will start.
items.feedback: Correct! Time clause 'As soon as' + Present.

items.questionText: If I had a car, I ___ drive to work.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Could' is the past of 'Can' and works like 'Would' here.

items.questionText: I wouldn't do that if I ___ you.
Unless he ___ sorry, I won't forgive him.
If she ___ the answer, she would tell us.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Would tell' indicates Second Conditional -> Past Simple 'Knew'.

items.questionText: He will be angry if you ___ late.
If I ___ in Cameroon, I would visit Kribi often.
I will wait until he ___.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Until' is a time connector. Use Present Simple for future.

items.questionText: If we lived in Paris, we ___ speak French every day.
You won't succeed ___ you work hard.
items.feedback: Correct! 'You won't... if you don't work hard' = 'Unless you work hard'.

items.questionText: If I ___ you were coming, I would have baked a cake.
items.feedback: Correct! Third Conditional (Past Regret): 'Would have baked' -> 'Had known'.

items.questionText: If you boil water, it ___ into steam.
If I ___ time tomorrow, I will help you.
If I ___ seen you, I would have said hello.
items.feedback: Correct! Third Conditional: If + Past Perfect (had seen).

items.questionText: ___ I known about the party, I would have come.
items.feedback: Correct! Inverted Third Conditional (Had I known = If I had known).

items.questionText: If you ___ told me earlier, I could have helped.
___ I to lose my job, I would be in trouble.
items.feedback: Correct! Inverted Second Conditional (Were I to lose = If I lost).

items.questionText: If I hadn't eaten lunch, I ___ hungry now.
items.feedback: Correct! Mixed Conditional: Past cause (hadn't eaten) -> Present result (would be).

items.questionText: ___ you see Paul, tell him to call me.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Should' inversion for First Conditional (Should you see = If you happen to see).

items.questionText: I would have passed the exam provided that I ___ studied.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Provided that' acts like 'If'. Third conditional logic applies.

items.questionText: If it ___ for the rain, we would have gone out.
items.feedback: Correct! 'If it hadn't been for' (Third conditional structure for 'Without').
items.subTopic: Fixed Expression (If it hadn't been for)

items.questionText: I wish I ___ taller.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Wish' + Past Simple (Were) for present regrets.

items.questionText: I wish I ___ harder for the test.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Wish' + Past Perfect for past regrets.

items.questionText: Suppose you ___ a million dollars, what would you do?
items.feedback: Correct! 'Suppose' acts like 'If'. Second conditional context (What would you do).

items.questionText: But for his help, we ___ failed.
items.feedback: Correct! 'But for' = 'If it hadn't been for'. Implies Third Conditional.

items.questionText: If I ___ rich, I wouldn't be working here.
items.feedback: Correct! Mixed Conditional: Present state (If I were rich generally), Present result.

items.questionText: Find the error: "If I would have known, I would have called."
items.feedback: Correct! Error: 'Would' in If-clause. Should be 'If I had known'.

items.questionText: If it ___ for your advice, I would have failed.
items.feedback: Correct! Third Conditional 'If it hadn't been for'.

items.questionText: I would rather you ___ now.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Would rather' + Person + Past Simple (Unreal present).

items.questionText: It's time we ___ home.
Had he studied, he ___ passed.
We will stay inside ___ it stops raining.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Until' connects the future action to the time limit.

items.questionText: If you ___ to see him, give him my regards.
items.feedback: Correct! 'If you happen to...' implies chance. Present simple.

items.questionText: If I eat too much, I ___ sick.
If he ___, I will go.
You will be cold if you ___ a jacket.
items.feedback: Correct! Negative condition in Present Simple.

items.questionText: Unless it ___, we will play football.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Unless it rains' = 'If it does not rain'.

items.questionText: If you mix yellow and blue, you ___ green.
I ___ buy a car if I have money.
If the phone rings, ___ it.
If we ___ the game, we will celebrate.
Ice melts if you ___ it.
If you ___ to bed late, you will be tired.
Unless he ___, we will start without him.
If I ___ early, I will cook.
When you ___ the button, the machine starts.
items.feedback: Correct! 'When' functions like 'If' in Zero Conditional here.

items.questionText: If she ___, she will pass the exam.
We will stay home if it ___.
If you are tired, ___.
If they ___ now, they will arrive on time.
You will get sick if you ___ that.
I ___ tell anyone if you tell me the secret.
If the light is red, ___.
If I ___ a bird, I would fly.
She would help if she ___ time.
If I ___ the answer, I would tell you.
Where ___ you go if you had a plane ticket?
We will leave as soon as he ___.
items.feedback: Correct! Time clause (As soon as) + Present.

items.questionText: If it ___ so cold, we would go swimming.
If I won the lottery, I ___ build a school.
Unless you ___ now, you will be late.
If I didn't have to work, I ___ come.
If he ___ younger, he would play.
What would you do if you ___ a snake?
items.feedback: Correct! Past Simple 'Saw' for imaginary condition.

items.questionText: I ___ happy if you came.
If you ___ the dishes, I will cook.
If I ___ there, I would tell him.
When the rain ___, we can go out.
You won't pass ___ you study.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Unless you study' = 'If you don't study'.

items.questionText: If you ___ me, I would help you.
If I had studied, I ___ passed.
items.feedback: Correct! Third Conditional (Had studied -> Would have passed).

items.questionText: If we ___ a taxi, we will arrive sooner.
If you ___ water, it becomes ice.
If she ___ the bus, she would have been late.
___ we arrived earlier, we would have met him.
If I had been hungry, I ___ eaten.
___ I to win the lottery, I would travel.
If I ___ earlier, I wouldn't be tired now.
items.feedback: Correct! Mixed: Past cause (had slept) -> Present result.

items.questionText: ___ you need help, just ask.
You can go out provided that you ___ early.
If it hadn't been for him, we ___ lost.
items.subTopic: Fixed Expression (If it hadn't been for)

items.questionText: I wish I ___ a car.
I wish I ___ to the party yesterday.
Suppose you ___ a job, what will you do?
But for the traffic, we ___ arrived on time.
If I ___ you, I would not do that.
Find the error: "If I would see him, I would tell him."
items.feedback: Correct! 'Would' in if-clause is wrong. Use 'saw'.

items.questionText: If only I ___ listened to my father.
I'd rather you ___ tomorrow.
It's high time we ___.
___ he worked, he would have succeeded.
items.feedback: Correct! Inverted Third Conditional 'Had he worked'.

items.questionText: If I ___ taller, I would play basketball.
If you ___ to arrive early, wait for us.
